summary: No public source found in this bounded search that supplies facility-specific, versioned clinical pathways with prerequisites, recovery stages, staffing, and case-specific timing for RWJUH (CCN 310038), Saint Peter’s (310070), or Middlesex County. The strongest complementary finds are national code classification and utilization references. They can help map procedures and provide limited utilization context, but do not establish clinical pathways or local operational standards. Sources are discovery leads; none is marked acquired.

sources.title: Clinical Classifications Software Refined (CCSR) for ICD-10-PCS Procedures, v2026.1
sources.publisher: Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality, HCUP
sources.geography: National coding classification; not facility- or county-specific
sources.period: v2026.1; valid for ICD-10-PCS codes through September 2026; released November 19, 2025
sources.grain: ICD-10-PCS code to one mutually exclusive CCSR category, with category and clinical-domain reference information
observed_facts: AHRQ states the tool maps over 80,000 ICD-10-PCS codes into more than 320 categories across 31 clinical domains.
The downloadable ZIP includes a CSV mapping, SAS mapping program, and documentation; the reference workbook includes category and code-mapping tabs.
AHRQ cautions the tool does not identify combinations of codes that together define complex procedures.
sources.retrieval_next_step: For a bounded mapping supplement, download the v2026.1 ZIP or reference workbook from the official page, preserve the release/version and source URL, and map only the ICD-10-PCS codes occurring in the already-acquired FY2024 DRG records. Keep mappings as coding classifications; do not treat them as DRG-to-procedure equivalence or a pathway.
limitations: National coding taxonomy, not clinical decision guidance or a pathway.
No indication, contraindication, consent, recovery, staff, resource, or minute-level timing fields.
The tool is distributed as a SAS program and mappings; local implementation may require adapting the input array.
Does not resolve complex procedures encoded by multiple procedure codes.

sources.title: Medicare Outpatient Hospitals by Provider and Service (public use file)
sources.geography: U.S. hospitals, including New Jersey where released; facility-level results may be filtered by provider ID
sources.period: Public use file versions listed for 2019, 2021, and 2023; methodology PDF inspected describes 2015–2022 data
useful_fields: outlier service count and average outlier payment
observed_facts: CMS describes the public use file as free and lists 2019, 2021, and 2023 versions.
CMS methodology specifies provider × C-APC aggregation and says records derived from 10 or fewer services are suppressed.
The file covers fee-for-service Medicare OPPS beneficiaries and selected C-APCs; it excludes Medicare Advantage and other payer groups, and is not a full hospital procedure census.
sources.retrieval_next_step: Download one listed year’s public use file and data dictionary through the CMS dataset page; filter by the two named facilities’ identifiers after checking the provider identifiers in the file. Save the selected year, dictionary, suppression status, and methodology with the source record. Use counts/payment fields only as limited Medicare outpatient utilization context, not as pathway duration, resource consumption, or total facility volume.
limitations: CMS data page was returned by search but opened as a one-line dynamic page; exact direct download URL was not independently verified, so the dataset page is the verified retrieval entry point.
Only selected outpatient C-APCs; not inpatient pathways and not all outpatient services.
Medicare fee-for-service population only; not necessarily representative of each hospital’s population.
Suppression and aggregation prevent inference of case-level sequences, prerequisites, or recovery.

sources.title: Integrated Outpatient Code Editor (I/OCE) Quarterly Release Files
sources.geography: National Medicare outpatient coding and payment edits; not geographically specific
sources.period: Quarterly releases; page inspected listed 2024 releases V25.R0, V251.R0, V252.R0, and V253.R0, along with later versions
sources.grain: Versioned code/edit and software release files used to process outpatient claims under OPPS and specified non-OPPS settings
useful_fields: outpatient code editor data and edit specifications
observed_facts: CMS describes the files as draft and final quarterly instructions and specifications for hospital outpatient departments and other specified provider settings.
The CMS page lists quarterly data files and software packages, including releases for 2024.
sources.retrieval_next_step: Open the CMS quarterly release page, select only the release matching the intended historical claim period (for a 2024 outpatient coding crosswalk, select the applicable 2024 quarter), and download its data files and documentation. Record the release ID and effective dates. Use only to validate coding/edit context for outpatient claims; do not translate edits into clinical appropriateness or pathway rules.
limitations: Coding/payment edit reference, not a clinical pathway.
No facility-level utilization or clinical timing fields.
Quarter-specific release selection matters; version must match claim period.
A direct file URL was not extracted; the verified page provides the downloadable release links.

missing_inputs: No public local pathway documents or local procedure-stage time/resource observations were verified for RWJUH or Saint Peter’s.
No independently verified local quantitative data for procedure prerequisites, recovery stages, staffing requirements, equipment quantities, or minutes.

For the two pathway dossiers, select case families present in the acquired FY2024 DRGs, then independently identify public professional-society or government clinical pathway sources and record applicable versions, indications, variants, contraindications, and consent requirements.

Any operational minutes, staffing counts, or resource quantities will require local workflow evidence or explicit simulation assumptions; keep assumptions separate from cited clinical rules and mark clinical reviewer as pending.
simulation_use: Use the AHRQ mapping to classify existing ICD-10-PCS codes and explore candidate case families without treating any DRG as a procedure. Optionally use CMS outpatient C-APC counts and payment summaries as narrowly scoped Medicare outpatient context. Do not calibrate pathway decisions, recovery, staffing, resource quantities, or procedure durations from these datasets. Build candidate dossiers only after selecting two supported case families and finding versioned primary clinical references; label operational timing/resource values as assumptions until local evidence or review is available.
limitations: This is bounded discovery, not dataset acquisition; no files were downloaded.
Only three source candidates are included. The CMS outpatient public-use file’s exact downloadable asset URL was not verified because its dynamic page could not be inspected beyond the search result.
The inspected sources do not provide a local New Brunswick/Middlesex clinical pathway dataset.
AHRQ CCSR mappings, CMS APC groupings, and DRGs are distinct classifications and must not be treated as interchangeable procedure definitions.
Clinical rules and operational assumptions remain unreviewed; no clinical reviewer is named.
